HERMAN MASHABA - THE ACCIDENTAL MAYOR

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Herman Mashaba, former mayor of Johannesburg reveals all in a new book that slams the liberals in the DA, exposes the ANC snakes in the city and implicates two current cabinet ministers in corruption.

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche will be first TV to reveal the behind the scenes look at what happened when Mashaba resigned suddenly from the DA in October last year, what was found at the City of Johannesburg, the sabotage and the allegations of corruption that he levels at two cabinet ministers - Ayanda Dlodlo and Lindiwe Sisulu

Summary:
Herman Mashaba’s stint as the disruptive DA mayor of Johannesburg since 2016 ended badly three years later when he resigned in October last year after Helen Zille was elected DA federal council chair. Now he is on the cusp of launching a new political party that will contest seats in the 2021 upcoming local government elections.

In a one on one interview with Masa Kekana, Mashaba and his chief of staff Michael Beamont will take us through the state of the city of Johannesburg, which Mashaba has dubbed the snake pit – the looting that had taken place, the outright sabotage of their every attempt to clean up the R35 billion rand of corruption that had brought the city to its knees, and how he kept together the most fragile coalition of opposition parties.



Further information:
Further information
The interview will also explore how Mashaba found a way to work with the EFF, and the irony that the most difficult coalition partner that he says finally brought about the downfall of the delicate arrangement was in fact his own party, the DA. “It was infuriating and disappointing that Mashaba was left to manage this nearly impossible coalition without the support of his own party.’ According to his chief of staff Michael Beamont

The story will also look at his view of what is wrong with local government, how his resignation led to the ANC back in charge, and how the measures his administration put in place to turn the city around are now threatened once again. For example the recent resignation of the chief of police David Thembe.

As disillusionment with both the ANC and the DA becomes a more prominent feature of our future politics, Mashaba predicts that coalitions will become the norm and the future of our politics could change dramatically by 2024.

The story will also include comments from smaller players that kept the coalition going, people like the IFP’sMzobanzi Ntuli and the EFF’s Musa Novela.

Press Release:


The Disruptive Mayor
Herman Mashaba’s term as the disruptive DA mayor of Johannesburg since 2016, ended abruptly when he resigned in October last year. Now he is on the cusp of launching a new political party that will contest seats in the 2021 local government elections. Now Mashaba takes Carte Blanche through those tumultuous three years of resistance to his corruption busting efforts; coalition politics; his current relationship with the DA, and what went wrong between himself and the party’s federal council chair, Helen Zille.
Producer: Joy Summers | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


Accidental Mayor Final Script FOR TX SUNDAY 7th JUNE 2020

Commentary One
When Herman Mashaba was elected as Johannesburg’s DA mayor in 2016, Michael Beaumont became his chief of staff, and so began a journal of their days in office.

MICHAEL
it was never intended as a book. I think in many ways the kind of daily chaos that was part of this job, just required an outlet.

Commentary Two
It tells a story of three years of resistance, sabotage, DA politics, allegations of ANC corruption, and Mashaba’s efforts to improve Johannesburg. For him, every day was like going to war

Herman
I was nervous. Nervous of running a multiparty government including the EFF. So, this was a dreadful job for me, and I can tell you it became much worse than I ever could have imagined. Do I regret it? Absolutely not.

Commentary three
Johannesburg had been promoted as a World Class African city by the ANC administration. That campaign cost almost R200 million rand. But instead Mashaba says, he found a slum.

Herman
and I used to say to the residents my goodness is this a world class African city where people do not have toilets, do not have water.

Michael
We walked into a city that was just dysfunctional. Because the infrastructure in Johannesburg was collapsing. You know the electricity substations were on the brink of turning off, we had transformers older than our grandparents, 75, 80 years old, the water pipes leaked like sieves. I mean city was losing 45% of its water every single year, 108 billion litres of water and that is just money just pouring into the ground, and while all of this going on, you have a level of looting and corruption that is going on in the city. So, we walked into a nightmare

Commentary Four
They also discovered what Mashaba describes, as outright, shameless, looting

Herman Mashaba
we were under impression that Jacob Zuma was the only captured one, we never thought the ANC in Gauteng was captured. The city of Johannesburg was right in the middle of the Gupta capture.



LINK
He knew there would be resistance, but he was shocked by the levels of sabotage and what he calls the snakes in the city council

Herman
I tell you! When I took over, everyone warned me about all the senior people, are all senior ANC people. All the departments literally

MICHAEL
Johannesburg was the crown jewel, and losing it was a deeply painful thing for the ANC. From day one they wanted the city back. They made it known, what they didn’t say they was that they would be actively working, to make sure of it

Commentary five
Beaumont describes instances of sabotage, how documents were hidden from them, and how they couldn’t even get sight of their own budget, but Mashaba was undeterred

Herman
Unfortunately, some really decided to really work for Luthuli house, than actually work for the City of Johannesburg. I used to say to them if you want to work for a political party then Luthuli House is walking distance away from here, going work for Luthuli House.

Commentary Six
But resistance to the new administration didn’t just come from inside council. Beaumont writes that organs of state weaponised against them

Masa
In chapter 12 you talk about the state versus Machaca?
Michael
You know the state became very effective at waging a war against the city of Johannesburg
money that had traditionally been given as grants to the city were being cut left right and centre -It was just at every level and it was systematic, and it could only be systematic like that across all these different spheres of government and organs of state if it is coordinated.

Commentary seven
Meanwhile across the city more and more evidence of corruption emerged. From former executives of City power, right down to substations, like this unfinished one in Eldorado park

Herman
We've already paid R66 million to the company and there is no substation. I said no guys it's is not possible.



Commentary eight
Mashaba soon knew he needed an entire unit to deal with the allegations of corruption and he chose former Hawks General Shadrack Sibiya to lead it. By May 2019, writes Beaumont there were over 6000 cases, and R35 billion rand under investigation.

Michael
You know what we had was a criminal justice system that would not lift a finger to help our efforts to fight corruption.

Commentary nine
Johannesburg is buckling under the pressure of migration and a housing backlog of 300 000.
And the inner -city renewal project became Mashaba’s obsession.

Up sound rain at night

500 hijacked buildings were identified for renewal, but that meant removing many illegal immigrants and that soon earned him the title of Xenophobe

Masa: Herman are you xenophobic?
Herman:
It's actually an insult when one sees the exploitation of our people.

Commentary Ten
He says he came across terrible cases of child trafficking and prostitution inside these buildings and he’s unapologetic about wanting to clean up the city

Mashaba
People are coming into our country illegally buying South African citizenship through fraudulent means, and you raise these matters and then you're called xenophobic

Commentary eleven
Some-how he managed to convince both the private sector and his coalition partners to develop 154 buildings into affordable accommodation

HERMAN
Hundred and fifty- four buildings to the value of R32 billion were already awarded to the private sector, I hope that project is not going to stop

Commentary twelve
But it looks like that is exactly what has happened. Because a year after Herman Mashaba did a sod turning event here, it’s still being used as a parking lot

Herman Mashaba
As you can see its idle when you have people with no houses, how come we have not really begun.

Commentary Thirteen
Governing the city writes Beaumont would have been impossible without the regular support of council

LINK
To get anything done anything in council Mashaba needed his six coalition partners on board and the support of the EFF, to say it was fragile is an understatement

Commentary fourteen
The EFF had initially rejected Mashaba, but he worked hard to bring them on board and later became known as the EFF mayor

Herman
One thing for sure without any doubt, the EFF where the most supportive of all the political parties

Commentary fifteen
But many in the DA were uncomfortable with that relationship

Michael
We found that the DA was the most difficult coalition partner in this arrangement

Herman:
I believe they were not happy with us and the EFF and our pro- poor policy, spending money in poor areas, instead of focus on cutting grass in the suburbs and so forth

Commentary sixteen
But Mashaba was allowing the EFF to dictate terms and losing DA voters, says Helen Zille

Helen Zille
And from very near the beginning Herman Mashaba became more beholden to the EFF than to the DA and I am told he regularly came into the DA caucus and said he had already reached agreement on any issue, the budget or anything else with the EFF and the DA would have to go along. So what Herman Mashaba did was bring the EFF into government through the back door and that was a betrayal of DA voters, and the ultimate betrayal was resigning and giving the city to the ANC

Commentary seventeen
Mashaba had planned to stay on as Mayor till 2021, but then he heard that some DA caucus members were about to vote to remove him

Herman
I said look, because you're planning to collapse this government, let me to move aside and that's a decision that I had to take because I was going to be removed any way.



Commentary eighteen
Ironically, in March last year Herman Mashaba said: In all the years I have known Helen Zille, including reading extensively about her beautiful life anyone calling her racist is actually racist themselves. Seven months later, when Zille was elected chair of the Federal council of the DA, he accused her of being right wing.

Herman
So, I said to them guys just note that if Helen is elected, if this right-wing element come back to take over the D.A. I am out.

Commentary nineteen
On October 21st last year Mashaba resigned from the DA and the City

Helen Zille
I had nothing to do with any decisions pertaining to the city of Johannesburg and governments arrangements there, however a large proportion of DA public representatives did not think it was a good idea to bring the EFF into executive government to stabilise coalitions, and to oppose that kind of arrangement does not make one right wing

Commentary twenty
Six weeks later the ANC’s Geoff Makluba was elected the new mayor

Masa: Now the very thing you set out to do which is unseat the ANC in the city of Johannesburg is exactly where we are today. Was it all for nothing?
Herman:
While it is really very unfortunate, more especially for me.

Commentary Twenty-one
Mashaba says his team had investigated Makhubo for corruption and laid criminal charges against him. He believes the current mayor wrongly benefitted to the tune of R30 million in fees from a City contract with Regiments – a Gupta linked company. Regiments did not answer our specific questions

HERMAN
Here is someone with overwhelming evidence reported to the ANC by the ANC still have the audacity to put him forward to be the mayoral candidate. I said My country is in trouble.

Commentary twenty- two
Mayor Makhubo responded that he was leading the City’s Covid19 Response and would not be distracted by Mashaba’s unsubstantiated allegations which he has made for the past three and a half years.

“Mr. Mashaba has left the city in a mess, evidenced by the R3 billion in unauthorised, irregular, fruitless and wasteful expenditure in 2018/2019. The mayor is as we speak, sitting with a damning report from Treasury on a R1.2 billion fleet contract that’s been found to be irregular. That is the legacy of the Mashaba years in office.”

Masa:
We have local government elections coming up and you have formed the people's dialogue.. Why would you want to go back into public office?
Herman:
What happened Masa upon announcing my resignation there was an outcry. People saying please stay on. Please form your own political party

Commentary twenty- three
In August Mashaba will launch his party and is planning on contesting Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni in the local government elections next year. Mashaba is hoping to return to lead Johannesburg, to finish what he started.

THE END 11 04.

PROMO ONE
What happened behind the scenes of the DA mayor Herman Mashaba’s administration? A new book written by his former chief of staff, Michael Beaumont reveals their story.

PROMO TWO
Corruption, sabotage, fractious politics and a city falling apart. Former DA mayor of Johannesburg Herman Mashaba’s account of a tumultuous three years in office.

PROMO THREE
Herman Mashaba’s term as the disruptive DA mayor of Johannesburg , ended abruptly when he resigned in October last year. Now he is on the cusp of launching a new political party.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Herman Mashaba, former mayor of Johannesburg reveals all in a new book that slams the liberals in the DA, exposes the ANC snakes in the city and implicates two current cabinet ministers in corruption.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche will be first TV to reveal the behind the scenes look at what happened when Mashaba resigned suddenly from the DA in October last year, what was found at the City of Johannesburg, the sabotage and the allegations of corruption that he levels at two cabinet ministers - Ayanda Dlodlo and Lindiwe Sisulu
metadata.Summary: Herman Mashaba’s stint as the disruptive DA mayor of Johannesburg since 2016 ended badly three years later when he resigned in October last year after Helen Zille was elected DA federal council chair. Now he is on the cusp of launching a new political party that will contest seats in the 2021 upcoming local government elections. In a one on one interview with Masa Kekana, Mashaba and his chief of staff Michael Beamont will take us through the state of the city of Johannesburg, which Mashaba has dubbed the snake pit – the looting that had taken place, the outright sabotage of their every attempt to clean up the R35 billion rand of corruption that had brought the city to its knees, and how he kept together the most fragile coalition of opposition parties.
metadata.Further information: Further information The interview will also explore how Mashaba found a way to work with the EFF, and the irony that the most difficult coalition partner that he says finally brought about the downfall of the delicate arrangement was in fact his own party, the DA. “It was infuriating and disappointing that Mashaba was left to manage this nearly impossible coalition without the support of his own party.’ According to his chief of staff Michael Beamont The story will also look at his view of what is wrong with local government, how his resignation led to the ANC back in charge, and how the measures his administration put in place to turn the city around are now threatened once again. For example the recent resignation of the chief of police David Thembe. As disillusionment with both the ANC and the DA becomes a more prominent feature of our future politics, Mashaba predicts that coalitions will become the norm and the future of our politics could change dramatically by 2024. The story will also include comments from smaller players that kept the coalition going, people like the IFP’sMzobanzi Ntuli and the EFF’s Musa Novela.
